## Course essentials

* **Instructor:** Prof. Rebecca Hutchinson. Office hours by appointment; please reach out.
* **Meetings:** Tuesdays and Thursdays (time and room on Canvas).
* **Credits:** 3
* **Prerequisites:** Graduate standing and some prior programming experience. Labs are offered in R and in Python; see [Get set up](setup.qmd).
* **Textbook:** None. Readings are provided (see [Readings](readings.qmd)).

### How you'll be assessed

| Component | Weight | What it involves |
|---|---:|---|
| Discussions | 30% | A post on (usually) one paper before each class meeting. Assesses learning outcomes 1–2. |
| Hands-on exercises | 30% | The [labs](labs/index.qmd); you report on each one in a Canvas discussion post. Assesses outcomes 2–3. |
| Term project | 40% | Build an SDM either on simulated data provided by the instructor (evaluated on withheld data) or on your own data. Includes a proposal, progress report, peer review, presentation, and final report. Assesses outcomes 3–4. |

Labs are usually due at 11:59 pm on the Wednesday after they're introduced. Late work: 0–24 hours late earns 90% credit and 24–48 hours late earns 50%. Contact the instructor about special circumstances.

**Generative AI:** use it judiciously to support the learning process, never to supplant it. See the AI guidance document on Canvas for specifics.
